question: In mathematics, there is an important difference between a "ratio" and a "proportion" when looking at a group of items. Which of the following statements correctly explains how a proportion works?
options: A proportion compares one specific part of a group to the total size of the whole group.
A proportion compares one part of a group directly to another part of the group.
A proportion always subtracts the parts to find a remaining whole number.
A proportion only tells you the total number of items in the group.

State whether the following mathematical statement is True or False:
14 ∶ 21 = 20 ∶ 40
options: True, because both ratios simplify to 1:2.
True, because both ratios simplify to 2:3.
